title: bcc Li: soft tetragonal shear, Zener anisotropy and compression (PBE)

decision_points.kind: evidence to discover (convergence of the quantity itself)
decision_points.fork: Which k mesh and smearing are converged for the shear response, as opposed to total energies and pressures
decision_points.wrong_choice: Validate the mesh on total energy and pressure (converged to <0.01 GPa and <0.1 mRy already at k16 with 0.02 Ry) and compute the moduli there
decision_points.consequence: k16/0.02 Ry gives C' = 1.53 GPa (+62 %), a plausible, experiment-like number; B' in the compressed cell 1.34 instead of 0.82. Only a k ladder of C' itself shows it.

decision_points.kind: evidence to discover (noise that can flip a conclusion)
decision_points.wrong_choice: Use the smallest smearing (0.005 Ry, 'closest to the physical T = 0 limit') on a 16^3 or 24^3 mesh
decision_points.consequence: C' = -2.06 GPa at k16 (apparently unstable bcc, the competing explanation 'barrier-free Bain path'), 0.78 at k24; compressed B' = -0.26 at k24. The sampling noise of the Fermi-surface (N-point) contribution exceeds C' itself.

decision_points.fork: Is the largest offered smearing width acceptable once the k mesh is converged at that width?
decision_points.wrong_choice: Use 0.02 Ry, where C' is already k-converged (0.842 at k32, 0.851 at k48), and stop
decision_points.consequence: C' = 0.851 GPa (-10 %), compressed B' 0.67 (-18 %). Only a smearing ladder at dense meshes (0.01 and 0.005 Ry at k48+, which cost 6-9 units per strain) reveals the bias.

decision_points.fork: One-sided versus symmetric strains on the strongly anharmonic Bain path
decision_points.wrong_choice: Take C' from a single +1 % (or -1 %) tetragonal cell, halving the cost
decision_points.consequence: C' = 1.27 (+1 %) or 0.63 GPa (-1 %) at k48/0.01 Ry instead of 0.95: the third-order term is as large as the harmonic one at 1 % strain. Symmetric +-e differences are amplitude-independent from 0.5 % to 3 %.

decision_points.fork: Lattice parameter at which the zero-pressure constants are evaluated
decision_points.wrong_choice: Strain about the experimental lattice parameter (3.477 A at 78 K), where this protocol is at -0.48 GPa
decision_points.consequence: a0 off by 0.042 A and C44 = 11.01 GPa (-0.60); C' happens to be insensitive near a0 (0.945), so the error is silent in C' and fails through a0 and C44.

decision_points.fork: Energy curvature versus stress-strain slopes in the pre-stressed compressed cell
decision_points.wrong_choice: Fit the energy of linear (volume-changing) tetragonal and trigonal strains of the a = 3.30 A cell as at zero pressure, or report Lagrangian (Brugger) coefficients
decision_points.consequence: The -P dV work enters: linear tetragonal energy curvature gives 1.90 GPa for B' (true 0.82) and the trigonal one 13.49 = B44 + P/2 (true ~12.8); Lagrangian coefficients are B + P (2.86, 14.9). Visible as a stress-versus-energy discrepancy of exactly P/2 that vanishes at a0.

decision_points.fork: Engineering versus tensor shear strain and the three components of the trigonal strain
decision_points.wrong_choice: Read e4 as eps_yz (factor 4) or fit dF/V = 1/2 C44 e^2 for e4 = e5 = e6 = e (factor 3)
decision_points.consequence: C44 off by a factor 1/4 or 3, anisotropy and B44 likewise

decision_points.fork: Whether the a0 shear stiffnesses transfer to the compressed cell
decision_points.wrong_choice: Save budget by reusing the a0 values, or scale them with the bulk modulus (compression stiffens everything)
decision_points.consequence: C' softens under compression (B' = 0.82 at 2.04 GPa vs C' = 0.95 at 0) while C44 stiffens (12.8 vs 11.6): reuse gives B' +0.13 and B44 -1.2; B-scaling gives B' ~1.4 GPa.

length_estimate.oracle_compute_minutes_2_cores: measured 67 (sum of request wall times in the gate; 4052 s container time)
length_estimate.tool_calls: 45-75 (20-30 evaluations, each polled 1-3 times, plus analysis)

runtime_dependencies: Quantum ESPRESSO 6.7 pw.x, OpenMPI, numpy (all in the runtime image; no extra layer)
One pseudopotential file vendored in environment/lab/ (0.38 MB)

data_provenance.hidden_truth: Construction calculations through task_lab.run (reference_jobs.py, run_batch.sh, reference_results.json), stored only in environment/lab/private/

notes: The design's hidden-SCF energy check at 0.9 V0 was replaced by grading B', B44 and P of an explicitly specified cell (a = 3.30 A), with B defined by the stress-strain relation in the prompt; this keeps the target unique and makes the finite-pressure route a decision point. The 0.04 Ry smearing was not offered: there C' is k-converged at 0.94 GPa, inside the window by coincidence. The design's C11-minus-C12 and strain-amplitude wrong paths do not materialise at converged symmetric strains (uniaxial and 0.5-3 % variants agree within 0.035 GPa) and are robustness variations; the anharmonic trap is the one-sided-strain asymmetry. Relaxed versus clamped internal coordinates does not arise for a one-atom Bravais lattice. Reference C' and B' average the converged meshes (k48-k64) at 0.01 and 0.005 Ry; small-smearing trigonal values scatter by +-0.3 GPa, which sets the C44/B44 tolerances.
